The Vims gauntlet

Each piece of the voxel life sim is rebuilt round after round until a blind critic picks our render over the reference. Last updated Oct 06, 23:09 UTC.

Characters

Round 2 · reference won
Critic verdicts (2)
  1. R2RefCharacters are far too small and stiff to read on a phone: at the home_day camera each person is only ~60-80px tall and the dog ~50px, standing upright in idle poses. The reference gets about 2x the screen height per character (move the camera closer/lower FOV or scale the rigs up ~1.6x) and poses each one in its activity: dad SEATED on the office chair turned 3/4 toward the camera so his beard, eyes and hair read (ours shows only his back); bunny-hat girl SEATED on a stool facing the easel holding the brush up; bear-hat kid SITTING cross-legged on the rug holding a toy; beagle LYING stretched out (front paws forward, head on bone, tail up) next to the ball, not standing upright. Also give faces bigger eyes/mouth voxels and warm rim light so they pop against the furniture.
  2. R1RefCharacters' poses/facing and head proportions: the dad at the desk is rendered from directly behind (no visible face/beard, just a brown hair block on a plaid back) and the music kid is a stiff standing figure whose oversized lavender hat-head is ~60% of her height and hides her face. Per the reference: rotate/turn the dad to 3/4 profile, seated with arms forward typing, so beard+face read; shrink kids' heads to ~1:1.5 head:body chibi with hat sitting ON the head (ears on top, face fully exposed below brim), and pose the music kid sitting cross-legged on the rug playing with toys, the painter seated on a stool facing the easel with brush arm raised, and the beagle lying down chewing a bone with clear floppy ears, white muzzle and tan patches instead of the hunched sitting blob.

HUD

Round 2 · reference won
Critic verdicts (2)
  1. R2RefWorld-anchored action bubbles float loose from their actors: the Work bubble and green plumbob hang ~100px above-left of the seated dad (over the monitor), and the Practice bubble plus '+ Music' chip hover far above the girl, so on a phone you can't tell which sim is doing what. Per the reference, anchor each bubble to the sim's head bone with a small fixed screen offset (~20-30px) so the tail tip touches just above the head, put the plumbob directly over the selected sim's head beside its bubble, stack skill chips just below/right of their bubble's tail, and shrink bubbles ~15% (smaller icon, tighter padding) so they don't dominate the scene.
  2. R1RefHousehold portrait cards (top-left): ours render the sim heads as small, soft, badly framed 3D captures - dad's face is cropped under hair, bunny-girl and cat-hat girl faces are tiny/washed out, dog is an unreadable smudge. Ref uses crisp, sharp, front-facing head-and-shoulders portraits filling ~85% of the white rounded card, face centred with clear eyes/smile, warm key light on a light backdrop. Fix the portrait camera (closer, eye-level, centred on face, no DOF/blur, higher render res). Secondary: action-bubble progress bars are stubby (~1/3 bubble width) and thin - make them span the full bubble width under the label, ~8px tall with rounded track like ref; add the missing season line under day/time in the clock panel.

House & lighting

Round 2 · reference won
Critic verdicts (2)
  1. R2RefRoom interiors are under-furnished, flat empty boxes, and there is no warm practical lighting. In OUR shot the upstairs rooms are mostly bare pale wall and floor, with a few tiny props: a small pink bed, scattered toy blocks, a near-empty bathroom with a lone shower box. The walls are tall plain slabs, and only 2-3 weak light glows show up. The reference fills every room edge to edge at a larger furniture scale. The pink bunny bedroom has a full canopy-height bed with a plaid quilt, a bedside table and lamp, wall shelves of books and plushies, framed bunny pictures, plants and a rug. The star-blue bedroom has a blue star quilt bed, bookshelf, globe, telescope, desk and string lights. The bathroom has a glass shower with a towel, a wood vanity with sink, mirror and plants, and a bath mat. Wall sconces every ~2m cast strong amber light pools (OmniLights with warm colour, about 2x energy plus shadows) on walls and floor. Fix: scale furniture up ~1.3x, add 8-12 props per room along the walls (shelves, frames, plants, lamps), add lit sconces and lamps with real light falloff, and cut the cutaway walls down to a low wainscot height so they show the interiors instead of blank plaster. Secondary: the background is an unreadable blue blur. It needs visible neighbour houses with lit windows, street lamps, trees and a moon, with less aggressive tilt-shift so the ground floor stays readable.
  2. R1RefCamera/framing and depth: ours is shot too close and top-down with no visible lower floor, so the railing borders blur instead of revealing the downstairs room; pull the home_day camera back and lower its pitch (~35-40 deg) to frame the whole upstairs open-plan room plus, past the balcony railing in the lower-left, a populated lower floor (bookshelves, table lamps glowing, sofa) like the reference. Also fill the bare floor/walls: add cork board with pinned notes and framed landscape painting above the desk, dual monitors+printer+mug on desk, tall bookshelf with globe/trophy, guitar next to keyboard, toy box and soccer ball, hanging vines. And cut the global orange/yellow grade (reduce saturation/warm tint and exposure, restore contrast and neutral wood tones; window should not blow out).

Backyard BBQ

Round 2 · reference won
Critic verdicts (2)
  1. R2RefDusk lighting + empty lawn: the centre/foreground is a huge bright saturated green grass plane with uniform daylight-style lighting and nothing on it. Per ref, darken/desaturate the grass to dusk blue-green, make every lantern, string-light bulb and the fire pit cast warm orange OmniLight pools (bulbs should glow/bloom, not be flat white squares), light the house back with glowing sliding glass doors showing furnished interior under the pergola deck, and fill the empty lawn with lush voxel flower mounds (purple/pink/white/yellow), stepping-stone path and lanterns so the table group fills the frame; also reduce the foreground DOF blur smearing the bottom third.
  2. R1RefSKY + BACKDROP: ours has no visible sky at all - the top third is a blurred flat dark-purple house wall/haze with no horizon. Pull the camera/house back or lower the house so a purple-to-orange sunset gradient sky (orange/pink glow at horizon, violet above, a few clouds) is visible across the top 20-25% of frame, and add a row of dark silhouetted voxel neighbour houses with a few warm lit windows plus dark tree silhouettes along the horizon behind the fence. Also reduce the purple DOF/fog wash on the house so its lit sliding glass doors (showing warm furnished interior) and pergola with string lights on posts read crisply.

Autumn festival

Round 2 · reference won
Critic verdicts (2)
  1. R2RefFALL TREATS stall (front-left) is an empty box: the sign text is clipped by the awning ('TREATS' cut off) and the counter shows no food and no vendor. Per ref, it should be a wooden stall with a red/white striped awning ABOVE a fully visible carved sign with a maple-leaf icon, plus a vendor NPC behind a counter piled with candy apples, pies and pretzels in trays. Secondary: pull the camera back and down so a clear cobblestone path leads to the fountain and a larger, lit stage with the guitarist. Thin out the giant leaf-block clusters that bury the top third of the frame, and remove the dark foreground lantern silhouette at bottom-center.
  2. R1RefBackground/midground is lost in a blown-out yellow-orange haze: bloom+glow and depth-of-field blur are far too strong, so the town hall/clock tower, bunting, stage and crowd are unreadable smears and the whole frame has no value contrast. Cut bloom/glow intensity and DOF far-blur drastically (keep only mild blur past the fountain), lower exposure so cobbles are mid-grey-brown not beige-white, and then actually populate the backdrop per ref: a red-brick town hall with a crisp white clock face framed by large saturated orange/red voxel tree canopies on both sides, a raised wooden stage at back-right with a guitarist, maple-leaf banner and triangle bunting, string lights with discrete warm bulbs, black lamp posts with glowing lanterns, and a stone fountain centre-midground.

Grocery market

Round 2 · reference won
Critic verdicts (2)
  1. R2RefCamera + lighting: ours uses a high top-down camera that fills half the frame with flat, evenly-lit beige floor, and has no visible pendant lamps or warm light pools. The reference uses a low, eye-level camera (about 1.6 m high, pitched only ~10-15 degrees down, FOV ~55) looking down the aisle so the background shows wood ceiling beams with rows of hanging pendant lamps (black shade + emissive warm bulb + omni light, bloom/glow), brightly glowing back-lit fridge cases full of bottles, and the signs hanging large above. Its checkout counter sits in the near foreground with depth-of-field blur. Fix: lower and pull the market preset camera to eye level aimed down the main aisle, add 6-10 pendant lamps with warm OmniLights and glow, make fridge interiors emissive white/blue, and add contact shadows/SSAO so the floor is glossy tile with warm pools of light instead of a flat plane.
  2. R1RefCamera/composition: the market preset camera sits too low and close, so the family fills the middle third and hides the store; the fridge cases, shelves and back aisles shrink to a thin distant strip. Per the reference, pull the camera back and up (about 1.6-2x the distance, looking down roughly 25-30 deg) so the characters are about 1/3 of the frame height, make the produce wall on the left readable as distinct voxel tomatoes/carrots/bananas/apples in crates with $ tags, show a full row of lit fridge cases with bottles and tall shelves of distinct cereal-box packs in the midground, add 3-5 background shoppers, and cut the heavy DOF blur and orange haze for brighter, neutral-warm lighting.

Game loop

Round 2 · reference won
Critic verdicts (2)
  1. R2RefAutonomy breaks across floors. The playtest step autonomy_arrives FAILS: a starving Maya (hunger 0.05) autonomously picks Cook on the Fridge, then is still in phase=walk 50s later at 3x speed. She ends at y 3.00 -> 0.00 and never reaches the fridge or starts acting. That is exactly the Sims 3 moment of a hungry sim going downstairs to eat, and here it silently fails. Fix it in scripts/sim/sim_agent.gd (walk/stair-following and arrival logic) together with scripts/sim/nav_grid.gd (inter-level stair links and the final approach cell in front of interactables): add stuck detection with a repath, then a fallback to the next-best target, and make arrival tolerant so a multi-level autonomous path reliably ends in phase=act. Next biggest gap: social is just one-shot Chat/Hug actions. There are no relationship meters, no friend/romance progression, no social menu tiers and no non-household townies to meet, so the Sims 3 relationship loop is missing. Build a per-pair relationship value in scripts/core/game.gd, shown in a Relationships tab of the HUD panel (scripts/ui/hud.gd), with socials in scripts/sim/sim_actions.gd that unlock by relationship level. Catalogue depth (~15 items, no walls or floors in Build) is also far from Sims 3.
  2. R1RefNo mood layer and no consequences: needs just decay as bars (game.gd NEED_DECAY) and nothing reads them except autonomy scoring, so there are no moodlets, no overall mood, and no failure (no passing out at 0 energy, no bladder accident, no hunger warning, no refusing actions). Skills also jump in big chunks (Music 0->0.75 in one short session) with no skill panel, and the queued orders (sim_agent.gd MAX_QUEUE=3) have no visible queue strip to tap and cancel. Build it as follows. Add a mood/moodlet system in scripts/core/game.gd: per member, a moodlets list of {id, icon, label, delta, expires}, an overall mood computed from needs plus moodlets, and a mood_changed signal. In sim_agent.gd, low needs push negative moodlets (Hungry, Tired, Bored, Smelly, Lonely), and completing actions, skill level-ups and tasks push positive ones (Well Rested, Had Fun, Learned Something). Mood scales skill gain and work pay, and need=0 forces an action (pass out / accident) that adds a strong negative moodlet. In scripts/ui/, add a mood plumbob colour (green/yellow/red) on plumbob.gd and portrait.gd, a moodlet row in need_panel.gd, a Sims-3-style action-queue strip of icons next to the selected portrait (tap to cancel), and a skills tab showing level 1-10 bars.
